text:
Noah Dobson's goal drought has become a Montreal talking point. He has none in 23 games this season, and Dose.ca counted 55 straight games without one going back into last season. Sportsnet wrote this week that the Canadiens need more from him.

Here's the case for patience. He has 3.1 expected goals and zero to show for it, and Montreal has scored eight fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. Our numbers flag both as the kind of luck that usually turns. He's playing 21 minutes a night, and the Canadiens break slightly better than even in expected goals with him out there. He has 9 assists, so he isn't invisible.

The case for worry comes from last season. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more chances with him on the ice than against all but 5% of defensemen, against top competition. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking also found that he shoots a lot but too few of his shots come from the slot. The first goal will come; we'd watch whether he gets closer to the net to find it.
headline: Noah Dobson is still waiting for his first goal
